label: Paddle
terms_note: Automation allowed with a Developer-tools API key (scoped permissions); MoR, 5 % + 50¢; rate limits per about/rate-limiting (429); payment domain must be approved before live checkout

sandbox.notes: Paddle Billing sandbox: 'API base URLs — Live https://api.paddle.com, Sandbox https://sandbox-api.paddle.com'. A separate sandbox account at sandbox-vendors.paddle.com with its own API key (keys contain _sdbx); no real payments; sandbox auto-approves refunds and retries webhooks on a shorter schedule.

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: Paddle API key (Paddle > Developer tools > Authentication; live keys look like pdl_live_apikey_...) sent as Authorization: Bearer. Give it product.read, product.write, price.write, transaction.read, adjustment.read and adjustment.write permissions for the full tool set. Sandbox keys (pdl_sdbx_apikey_...) need base https://sandbox-api.paddle.com, which this server does not switch to.

config_fields.name: tax_category
config_fields.help: Tax category for create_product (POST /products requires it): standard, digital-goods, ebooks, implementation-services, professional-services, saas, software-programming-services, training-services or website-hosting. Only create_product needs it.

adapter.terms: Paddle is the merchant of record; a refund adjustment on a live account is created with status pending_approval and reviewed by Paddle before it is processed (sandbox approves automatically).

me.note: GET /event-types (no specific permission listed) answers {data[{name, description, group, available_versions}], meta{request_id}}; it verifies the API key and the environment. Paddle has no account/me endpoint.

list_products.note: GET /products?include=prices&per_page (1-200, default 50)&status (active|archived; Paddle defaults to active). `price`/`currency` come from the product's first included price (unit_price.amount is a STRING in the currency's lowest denomination, e.g. "1000" = 10.00 USD; other prices stay in raw.prices). Paging is by cursor (`after` from meta.pagination.next), which page/limit cannot carry: `page` is ignored and only the first page is returned; `total` is not mapped (estimated_total may be -1).

get_product.note: GET /products/{product_id}?include=prices returns data{id, name, description, tax_category, type, image_url, custom_data, status, created_at, updated_at, prices[]}; `price`/`currency` are the first price's unit_price (amount as a string in the lowest denomination).

create_product.note: POST /products {name (required, 1-200 chars), description, tax_category (required by Paddle, taken from the tax_category setting; a 400 upstream_error means it is unset)}. Paddle products carry no price: `price`/`currency` are NOT sent — call update_price afterwards to create the price entity. The product is created active; `url` is not accepted (image_url is not a product page).

update_price.note: Paddle prices are separate entities, so this CREATES a new active price for the product with POST /prices {description (required internal note, fixed), product_id, unit_price{amount, currency_code}}; existing prices stay active until archived (PATCH /prices/{price_id} status=archived, not mapped). `price` is sent as the documented STRING in the currency's lowest denomination — pass an integer such as 1000 for 10.00 USD (a decimal is rejected). `currency` is required by Paddle. The result's `id` is the product id; the new price id is raw.id (pri_...).

list_sales.note: GET /transactions?include=customer&per_page (max 30)&created_at[GTE]=since (RFC 3339), newest first (default order id[DESC]). `amount` is details.totals.total, a STRING in the lowest denomination after discount and tax; `product_id`/`product_name` come from the first line item's price. There is no product filter, so `product_id` is not sent. Cursor paging (`after`) cannot be carried by page/limit: `page` is ignored and only the first page is returned. `refunded` is not a transaction field (see list_refunds).

list_refunds.note: GET /adjustments?action=refund&per_page (default 10, max 50), newest first. `amount` is totals.total (string, lowest denomination); `status` is pending_approval, approved, rejected or reversed. The endpoint has no date filter, so `since` is not sent; chargebacks are action=chargeback (not listed here). Cursor paging: `page` is ignored, first page only.

refund.note: DESTRUCTIVE: POST /adjustments {action: refund, transaction_id: sale_id (txn_...), reason, type: full} requests a FULL refund of the transaction. `amount` is NOT sent and does not limit the refund: a partial adjustment needs items[{item_id, type, amount}] per transaction item, which this input cannot express — call the API directly for partial refunds. `reason` is required by Paddle (a missing reason is a 400 upstream_error). On live accounts the adjustment is created as pending_approval and reviewed by Paddle; sandbox approves automatically.

not_offered.get_sales_stats: No revenue-totals endpoint: the Reports API (POST /reports, then GET /reports/{report_id}/download-url) produces an asynchronous CSV report of transactions or adjustments rather than a totals object the runtime could map.

evidence: host api.paddle.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 8/8 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
spec https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PaddleHQ/paddle-openapi/main/v1/openapi.yaml: 8/8 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
